walkthroughs.h2: Why was the Berlin Wall built?
walkthroughs.body_html: Between 1949 and 1961 about 3.5 million East Germans fled through Berlin, including skilled professionals. Khrushchev's 1958 ultimatum demanding Allied withdrawal failed at the June 1961 Vienna summit. On 13 August 1961 East German forces sealed the border with wire, replaced by concrete. The Wall stabilised the GDR while becoming the Cold War's defining image until its fall on 9 November 1989.

After U-2 photographs revealed Soviet IRBMs in Cuba on 14 October 1962, Kennedy announced a 'quarantine' on 22 October. ExComm rejected airstrikes. On 27 October a U-2 was shot down and Khrushchev sent two contradictory letters. Robert Kennedy's secret deal with Dobrynin traded Jupiter missiles in Turkey. The crisis prompted the 1963 hotline and Test Ban Treaty.

US escalation from 1965 reached 543,000 troops by 1969. The Tet Offensive on 30 January 1968, though militarily defeated, eroded domestic support. Nixon's Vietnamization, secret Cambodia bombing and the 1972 Christmas bombing aimed to extract a face-saving peace. The Paris Accords of 27 January 1973 ended US combat; PAVN captured Saigon on 30 April 1975, reunifying Vietnam.

mcqs.q: What was the Tet Offensive's main significance?
options: The Tet Offensive was a military victory for the Viet Cong that drove out the US.
The Tet Offensive ended the Vietnam War in 1968.
Militarily the Viet Cong suffered heavy losses, but politically it shattered the US public belief that the war was being won, fuelling anti-war pressure on Johnson.
The Berlin Wall was built by NATO to keep East Germans out of West Germany.

mcqs.q: Why was the Berlin Wall built in 1961?
options: The Berlin Wall was built to stop a Western invasion of East Berlin.
The Berlin Wall was built by NATO to keep East Germans out of West Germany.
To stop the mass flow of East Germans to the West via Berlin (millions had fled), which was draining the GDR of skilled workers and threatening the regime's survival.
Stalin blockaded Berlin to stop Nazis escaping to the West.

mcqs.q: Why did Stalin blockade West Berlin in 1948?
options: Stalin blockaded Berlin to stop Nazis escaping to the West.
The Tet Offensive ended the Vietnam War in 1968.
Stalin blockaded Berlin because he wanted to invade Western Europe.
To force the Western Allies out of Berlin in response to the merging of their zones, introduction of the Deutschmark, and creation of a separate West German state.
